extracted.intended_audience: undergraduate students (discrete mathematics / computer science) assigned a historical-source project; instructors who will assign or evaluate such projects
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for completing a course historical project that examines a primary historical mathematical source: how to read the source, research background, perform computations/experiments to verify the source, answer project questions, and produce a final written paper connecting the historical material to modern techniques.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start early / work regularly
rubrics_metrics.description: Start today. This is a major assignment, requiring more work than most homework problems from a textbook. Work on the project every day before it is due.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat the project as a significant, ongoing task rather than last-minute work. Regular daily effort is expected and will be rewarded; procrastination is an anti-pattern.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey the whole project before diving in
rubrics_metrics.description: Read the entire project to see what is involved. From what time period is the historical piece? What modern topics have evolved from the source?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Begin with a high-level pass to understand scope, context, and connections to modern topics so you can plan research and identify relevant background material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Careful reading and vocabulary/notation comprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Next read the project very carefully and make a list of any unfamiliar words or concepts. Do you understand the language of the historical author? If not, ask your instructor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay attention to historical phrasing and nonmodern notation. Document unfamiliar terms and resolve them early (instructor, library, or vetted secondary sources). Misreading the language is a common source of error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplementary research with source evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: Feel free to seek additional historical or mathematical information about the source from either the library or the Internet. Always question the validity of Internet sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use libraries and reputable secondary sources to contextualize the primary source; when using web sources, verify credibility. Keep track of citations and be cautious of unsourced Internet material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Experiment and verify with your own calculations
rubrics_metrics.description: The historical presentation is often more verbal than modern textbook formulations ... you must carefully read the historical author’s words and be prepared to experiment with your own calculations to verify or amplify the historical source.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carry out sample computations, construct tables, and replicate the historical procedures to confirm interpretations. Use experimentation to illuminate ambiguous passages and to support claims in your write-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Answer questions completely and use mixed-mode exposition
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin answering questions in the project. Use complete sentences along with equations, tables, or diagrams to support your work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond to each question in full prose; integrate equations, tables, and figures where appropriate. Some questions are simple; others require detailed solutions—use appropriate mathematical formality and clear exposition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify difficult questions early and seek help
rubrics_metrics.description: Some questions will be rather simple, while others require detailed solutions. Identify the difficult questions early and seek help from your instructor if you don’t know how to proceed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize hard items so you have time to get guidance. Waiting until the last minute to ask for help is an anti-pattern that risks incomplete or incorrect solutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seek instructor feedback iteratively
rubrics_metrics.description: Seek feedback from your instructor even if you feel that you have answered the questions correctly, since you may have misinterpreted a passage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use instructor feedback as an essential step to catch misinterpretations and improve correctness; incorporate comments before finalizing the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final written paper: completeness, clarity, and modern framing
rubrics_metrics.description: The final solution to the project should be a written paper in which you address all the issues raised in the project. Use complete sentences along with modern equations to support your claims. Discuss any connections from the historical source with present-day techniques that you may have encountered. How does the historical source differ from the textbook presentation?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The deliverable must cover every required issue, present arguments in clear prose supported by modern notation, and include reflective discussion linking the historical material to contemporary concepts and highlighting differences from standard textbook treatments. Failure to address all issues or to modernize/interpret the source is a common deficiency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation artifacts: tables/diagrams/structured answers when requested
rubrics_metrics.description: For some tasks (example: weighing stones) make structured artifacts such as a table with one column for each standard weight and another column for the stone of unknown weight; place an 'X' in the columns for the standard weights used to weigh each stone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow specific formatting instructions in problem prompts (e.g., construct tables, mark used weights). Providing the requested structured artifacts demonstrates comprehension and attention to instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use modern notation where appropriate but recognize historical style
rubrics_metrics.description: Use modern equations to support your claims; the historical presentation is often more verbal than modern textbook formulations and may use nonstandard notation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Translate historical expressions into contemporary mathematical notation to clarify arguments and to facilitate verification, while noting any meaningful differences in notation or style found in the primary source.
